findings.issue: The two adapters return empty sets differently. If a caller stores an empty non-nil []VerbatimBlock{}, the memory adapter returns nil (factStoreCloneBlocks uses append onto nil) and SQLite returns []VerbatimBlock{} (JSON '[]'). Facts behave the other way round: the memory adapter keeps an empty slice. No covered requirement depends on this. It only matters if T4 or L3 tests compare against an empty slice with reflect.DeepEqual.
findings.fix: Optional: make factStoreCloneBlocks keep empty non-nil slices the way factStoreCloneFacts does (make + copy), so both adapters agree.

requirements_checked.evidence: Store side done; the Prepare wiring belongs to T4. internal/recipe/factstore.go:39-57 upserts one row per (tenant, actor, section) with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE, and factstore.go:115-121 overwrites the memory map entry. Proven for both adapters by TestFactStoreReplacesPreviousSet: a second set replaces the first and does not append, and a plain INSERT would fail with a primary-key conflict. Tenant isolation is covered by TestScenario7LatestFactsPerActorAndSection (the 'tenant-two' check). Persistence is covered by TestFactStoreSQLiteSurvivesReopen.
